paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: Single vs. multiple platforms as data sources over time. While most of the datasets are collected from a single source, around 2018 researchers are increasingly collecting data from multiple sources (i.e., two or more).
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets collected from single versus multiple platforms over time, spanning from 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the year, while the vertical axis indicates the number of datasets, ranging from 0 to over 100. Two categories are shown: datasets sourced from a single platform (labeled “1”, blue bars) and those from two or more platforms (labeled “2+”, orange bars). From 2012 to 2017, the number of datasets is low overall, with most sourced from a single platform. Starting in 2018, there is a noticeable upward trend in both categories, with the “2+” category growing more rapidly. In 2020, the “1” category peaks at approximately 85 datasets, while “2+” reaches around 45. In 2021, “1” reaches its highest point at over 110 datasets, and “2+” climbs to nearly 50. In 2022, both categories decline slightly, with “1” at about 30 datasets and “2+” at roughly 10. The chart visually supports the caption’s claim that while single-source datasets have historically dominated, multi-source data collection has become increasingly common since 2018.
